issues.legal_issue: A constitutional writ protecting possession cannot be issued when the claimant’s asserted right depends on a disputed title that the writ court has declined to determine and no other legal right has been established.
material_facts: The respondents sought writs to prevent the State from dispossessing them after it issued notices resuming the grants under which their predecessors had held the properties.
The respondents claimed the grants gave them proprietary interests, while the State contended that the grants were service tenures resumable at its will.
The High Court declined to decide the disputed nature of the grants and title in writ proceedings, but ordered that the respondents not be dispossessed except in due course of law.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was not justified in issuing the writs because the respondents had not established a legal right supporting that relief; the orders were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Article 226 permits relief beyond enforcement of fundamental rights, but a writ requires an established right that has been illegally invaded or threatened. A writ cannot be issued solely to provide interim relief; under State of Orissa v. Madan Gopal Rungta, interim relief must aid and be auxiliary to relief available after the rights are determined in the substantive proceeding.

rule.if: constitutional_writ_proceeding and title_claim_contested and title_not_determined and no_other_legal_right_established

predicates.constitutional_writ_proceeding: The claimant sought relief through a constitutional writ proceeding.
predicates.title_claim_contested: The parties disputed whether the claimant held title or another legal interest in the property.
predicates.title_not_determined: The court left the disputed title issue undecided in the proceeding.
predicates.no_other_legal_right_established: No other legal right supporting the requested relief was established in the proceeding.

issues.definition: When a writ proceeding leaves a contested title unresolved and establishes no other supporting legal right, writ relief is unavailable.

issues.legal_issue: Long possession under a grant that is resumable by the State does not by itself establish a right to remain in possession against the State as grantor.
material_facts: The respondents relied on their predecessors’ long possession of the properties granted by the State to support their claim to protection against dispossession.
The State asserted that the properties had been granted as remuneration attached to an office and were resumable; the terms and character of the grants had not been determined.
The respondents sought protection against the State in writ proceedings without establishing that the grants were not resumable.
issues.conclusion: Possession alone did not establish a right against the State sufficient to support a writ; such a right depended on establishing that the grants were not resumable.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 226, possession under a resumable grant does not confer a right against the State grantor that supports a writ after resumption, although long possession may protect a possessor against third parties. The Court assumed without deciding that relief analogous to that under Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act might be claimed under Article 226 against the State. It distinguished Kistareddy v. Commissioner of City Police, Hyderabad, Mohinder Singh v. State of Pepsu, and Mrs. C. N. Lloyd v. District Council, United Khasi and Jaintia Hills, which concerned possession disturbed by executive action not founded on law.

rule.if: constitutional_writ_proceeding and possession_derived_from_state_grant and grant_is_resumable and state_is_grantor

predicates.constitutional_writ_proceeding: The claimant sought protection through a constitutional writ proceeding.
predicates.possession_derived_from_state_grant: The claimant’s possession arose from a grant made by the State.
predicates.grant_is_resumable: The grant permits the State to resume the property.
predicates.state_is_grantor: The State seeking to recover possession is the grantor.

issues.definition: When possession in a writ proceeding derives from a resumable grant made by the State seeking possession, that possession alone does not establish a right against the State.
